guard: a CONSUMER.DELETE timeout during membership-watch disarm is best-effort cleanup, not a process kill
why: The live crash was TimeoutError from consumer.delete in disarmMembershipWatch on a live
observer. The old catch rethrew any timeout while the connection was still open.
A1 restores that live throw. A2 swallows the timeout without emitting the error event.
A3 shares the timeout predicate with #851: a probe timeout collapsed to `unreachable` again makes
the workspace preflight re-read INFO and report a CA problem for a slow link. It rebuilds core
first because the preflight suite imports workspace and core through their dist.
A3 declares no completion marker: the preflight suite is fail-fast, and its count line prints only
on a green run, so a marker there would grade every real kill INCONCLUSIVE.

mutations.name: A1 live delete timeout still throws, the measured crash
mutations.expectRed: a live delete timeout does not reject disarmMembershipWatch

mutations.name: A2 swallow timeout without surfacing an endpoint error
mutations.expectRed: the timeout is surfaced as an endpoint error event

mutations.name: A3 a probe timeout collapses to unreachable again, so a TLS-required target's slow link reads as a trust failure (#851)
mutations.find: if (e !== undefined && isTimeoutError(e)) return { ok: false, reason: "timeout" };
mutations.replace: if (e !== undefined && isTimeoutError(e)) return { ok: false, reason: "unreachable" };
mutations.expectRed: S11 held-open TLS peer: preflightTarget → slow-link, prune:false (#851 cell a)
